types.name: bool
types.description: Canonical logical false or true; never host truthiness.

types.name: error
types.description: Typed language error payload independent of a backend return convention.

types.name: panic-info
types.description: Typed catchable runtime panic payload on a channel disjoint from language errors and hard traps.

types.name: type-variable
types.description: Registry meta-type resolved by a verified function or block signature.

types.name: string
types.description: Immutable managed UTF-8 text: a valid UTF-8 byte sequence with an exact byte length; identity is unobservable and equality is by content.

types.name: rune
types.description: Exactly one Unicode scalar value in [0, 0x10FFFF] excluding the surrogate range [0xD800, 0xDFFF].

types.name: f64
types.description: IEEE-754 binary64 value; constant identity preserves all 64 bits, including signed zero and NaN payloads.

types.name: string-builder
types.description: Unique mutable managed text builder; affine owner with forbidden copy, borrowed mutation and independent immutable string snapshots. Physical storage is executor-private.

effects.name: call
effects.description: Invoke a sealed in-program function with its declared effects.

effects.name: target-query
effects.description: Read one immutable value from the bound XrTargetProfile.

effects.name: panic
effects.description: Typed catchable panic continuation publication, distinct from business errors and hard traps.

effects.name: suspend
effects.description: Cooperative transfer from a logical safepoint to its declared continuation state.

effects.name: provider-call
effects.description: Invoke one exact operation through the provider binding of the active execution instance.

effects.name: cancel
effects.description: Terminate a suspended coroutine through its explicit cancellation continuation.

traps.name: integer-overflow
traps.description: A checked signed integer result is outside [-2^63, 2^63-1].

traps.name: integer-division-overflow
traps.description: i64 minimum divided by -1 has no i64 result.

traps.name: explicit-trap
traps.description: The program explicitly publishes a deterministic trap.

traps.name: profile-unavailable
traps.description: The required immutable target-profile field is absent or invalid.

traps.name: variant-tag-mismatch
traps.description: A variant payload projection names a different variant than the value carries.

traps.name: provider-call-failed
traps.description: The admitted provider trampoline refused or failed the requested operation.

traps.name: module-slot-uninitialized
traps.description: A module slot value is read or replaced before its initializer publishes it.

traps.name: module-slot-already-initialized
traps.description: A module initializer attempts to publish the same slot twice.

determinism.allowed_trace: One exact quotient/remainder, or one panic carrying code420/421 and the declared preserved values; no result is published on the panic path.

One nonnegative i64 logical sequence length: Unicode scalar count for immutable UTF-8 strings, element count for arrays. Reading length is O(1); construction and copy maintain the count. No allocation, provider call, owner transfer, normalization or grapheme segmentation occurs.

One fresh affine array containing the ordered operands, including the empty sequence. Affine elements transfer exactly once; trivial values remain available. Allocation failure publishes no array and consumes no input owner.

For an array, fixed array or borrowed sequence view, evaluate source then signed i64 index. Admit exactly 0 <= index < logical length; negative indices are not end-relative. Success returns a non-owning place with the exact element type, original storage identity and write permission no stronger than the source. Failure publishes the language index-out-of-bounds panic, no place and no memory access, then follows the optional exact panic continuation or escapes. Construction does not allocate, copy or transfer an owner. Storage invalidation or root destruction while the place is live is forbidden. Slice-range normalization is a separate operation.

Create one fresh synchronized identity with exactly the declared scalar element value. The result is affine with identity-preserving explicit copy; no operand is consumed. Allocation failure publishes no handle and preserves input owners. Physical storage and reference counts are private to the executor.

Borrow a live Atomic identity and return one scalar value observed by a single atomic load. Ordering is 0:Relaxed, 1:Acquire, 2:Release, 3:AcquireRelease, 4:SeqCst; load maps Release to Relaxed and AcquireRelease to Acquire. Other encodings are rejected. Concurrent observations must admit a C11 linearization consistent with the selected ordering; the handle is neither copied nor consumed.

Borrow a live Atomic identity, atomically replace its exact scalar element, and return the actual previous value. Ordering is 0:Relaxed, 1:Acquire, 2:Release, 3:AcquireRelease, 4:SeqCst; other encodings are rejected. All aliases observe the same synchronized identity. Concurrent exchanges admit a C11 linearization consistent with the selected ordering. No allocation, deep copy or ownership transfer occurs.

Strong atomic compare-exchange on a live synchronized identity: compare exact scalar bits with expected, replace with desired only on equality, and return the actual previous scalar. No spurious failure. Success uses ordering 0:Relaxed, 1:Acquire, 2:Release, 3:AcquireRelease, 4:SeqCst; failure uses Relaxed. Other encodings are rejected. No allocation or ownership transfer occurs; concurrent calls admit a C11 linearization. The source success flag is derived by exact scalar equality against expected.

Linearizable synchronized scalar update, returning the actual old value. Control encodes mode*8+ordering: mode 0 adds, 1 subtracts, 2 XORs; ordering 0..4 denotes Relaxed, Acquire, Release, AcquireRelease, SeqCst. Other bits are rejected. i64 add/sub wrap modulo 2^64; bool only permits XOR with an exact bool operand. No allocation or ownership transfer occurs. All aliases observe one identity and concurrent operations admit a C11 linearization.
one exact IEEE-754 binary64 bit pattern
